content: Azelastine is an antihistamine medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms of hay fever and allergies, such as a runny nose, sneezing, and nasal itching. It may also be used for other purposes as determined by your doctor. Azelastine is administered as a nasal spray. Typically, it is sprayed into each nostril twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use azelastine exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Before using the nasal spray for the first time, remove the child-resistant screw cap and attach the pump unit. Prime the pump by spraying it four times or until a fine mist is produced. If you have not used the spray for three or more days, re-prime the pump with two sprays or until a fine mist appears. Before using azelastine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to azelastine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including other cold and allergy products, antihistamines, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using azelastine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using azelastine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you understand how it affects you. Additionally, alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of this medication, so exercise caution. If you miss a dose of azelastine, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not use a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Azelastine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: A bitter taste in the mouth Fatigue Weight gain Muscle pain Nasal burning sensation Store azelastine in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal methods. If a child accidentally ingests azelastine, contact a doctor or poison control center immediately. Keep all medical appointments while using this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Maintain a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, as well as any vitamins, minerals, or dietary supplements you are taking. Bring this list to all medical appointments and keep it with you in case of emergencies. Azelastine is available under the brand names Astelin® Nasal Spray and Astepro® Nasal Spray.
